typical_symptoms: Presence of red bugs and nymphs feeding on green and maturing bolls
Yellowish-brown staining of white cotton lint
Small puncture marks on young green bolls leading to internal boll rot
Loss of seed viability and reduced lint quality
visual_characteristics: Adult insects with vivid red to orange-red elongated bodies, black spots, and black wing membranes
Distinct white transverse bands or collars visible on the underside and thorax of the insect
Insects commonly observed mating end-to-end (tail-to-tail) on cotton bolls
Small dark pinpoint feeding punctures on green boll surfaces
Yellowish or brownish discolored cotton lint inside open bolls
lesion_characteristics: Pinpoint feeding punctures on boll surface
Depressed, dark necrotic spots at feeding sites
Internal segment necrosis without clear chlorotic halos
color_characteristics: Vivid red and orange-red insect body coloration
Black wing membranes and dark spots on elytra
White transverse bands across thorax and abdominal segments
Dark brown or black tiny feeding punctures on boll walls
texture_characteristics: Dry, shriveled, and hardened boll husks
Matted and sticky stained lint fibers
Rough, pitted outer surface on heavily punctured green bolls
spatial_patterns: Aggregated clusters of adults and nymphs on individual bolls
Scattered small feeding punctures across the outer boll surface
Patchy internal lint staining following insect feeding
distinguishing_features: Presence of bright red/orange bugs with black wing tips and white body bands
Insects frequently observed mating joined end-to-end on bolls
Characteristic yellow-brown lint staining caused by Nematospora fungal transmission during feeding
